voices.name: Brand
voices.description: Professional, informative, authoritative. Confident but not arrogant. Formal and precise, but formal with warmth — not casual, not stiff.
voices.best_for: All KORE content unless another format is specified

structure: BODY (3-5 H2 sections, one key idea each, reference a vertical or customer story where possible)
seo_rules: Primary keyword in title, first 100 words, at least 2 H2s, and conclusion
Meta description 150-160 characters including primary keyword
Flag internal links as [INTERNAL LINK: topic]
Flag external citations as [EXTERNAL LINK: source type]

deliverable_format: 1. Meta info block (title, meta description, primary keyword, target audience, word count)
2. Full content (formatted with H1, H2s, body)
3. SEO notes (keyword placement summary, internal/external link suggestions)
4. Editor notes (optional: flags for client review, suggested images, stat verification needed)
cta_examples: Ready to simplify your IoT deployment? Talk to a KORE expert.
gold_standard_writing_principles: Lead with the problem, not the product — every top piece opens with a business, operational, or human challenge, not a KORE capability
Earn the positioning — expertise comes through in the quality of the explanation, not explicit self-promotion
Be the trusted advisor — when two options exist, explain both fairly; when an answer depends on context, provide a framework, not a cop-out
Ground future-looking content in evidence — trend pieces cite what happened before predicting what's next
Make every paragraph independently useful — structure for scanning, snippet capture, and re-use
Match technical depth to the audience — OEM/product teams get operational depth, general business audiences get outcome framing
Use narrative for healthcare and event content — the human story carries health content, the ecosystem story carries event content
Never oversell a new standard or technology — accuracy is the credibility play
quality_checklist: Aligns with KORE voice and tone
Reinforces at least one messaging pillar (Flexible, Global, Scalable, Proven)
No unsubstantiated superlatives without a proof point
Primary keyword in title, intro, and conclusion
Cross-checked against the content library log for duplication (see blog_topics.md)
No competitor brand names unless explicitly a comparison piece
Checked against the 8 Writing Principles above as a final pass
